deterrence

/dih-TUR-uhns/ - the stress falls on TUR · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Deterrence means the practice of preventing an action by making its likely cost seem too high.

The city wall was deterrence in granite: in two centuries, no army arrived to test it.

Example

The hoverfly cannot sting anyone. It wears the wasp's yellow-and-black anyway, because the pattern does the work: a young bird pecks one wasp, remembers the jolt, and spends the rest of its life refusing anything striped. The fly has no weapon at all — only deterrence: the advertisement of a sting it does not own, worn where every sparrow can read it.

Deterrence is the exact word for those stripes, because deterrence is the practice of preventing an action by making its likely cost seem too high — the attack is priced out before it is tried. Defense would be the sting itself, paid out during the attack; deterrence is the warning label that makes the sting unnecessary.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

prevention: Prevention stops the act by whatever means come to hand — a wall, a lock, a guard — and it does not care what anyone was thinking. Deterrence works only inside the would-be actor's head: the act stays physically possible, and the likely cost alone makes it not worth choosing.

discouragement: Discouragement is the low-stakes everyday cousin of deterrence: no threat is posted, only dampened appetite — a sigh, a hard form, a cold reception. Deterrence names its stakes out loud and works by making the likely cost of an act too high to accept.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

encouragement: tilts the arithmetic the other way

invitation: prices the act at nothing and props the door open

Where it sits · how much free choice remains

warning → deterrence → coercion

warning vs. deterrence: A warning is lighter than deterrence — it points at a risk and leaves the whole choice in your hands, where deterrence loads the choice by making one side of it expensive.

coercion vs. deterrence: Coercion goes further than deterrence — deterrence leaves you free to walk away from the act; coercion twists your arm until you perform one.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — de-: away from

Root — terr: to frighten (Latin terrere)

Suffix — -ence: the practice or state of

Put it together: De- (away from) + terr (to frighten) + -ence (the practice of) = the practice of frightening away. It is this unit's deter dressed as a noun and made standing policy: not one scare, but a posted, permanent one — the stripes the whole hedgerow can read.

Use the root in a new word: terror: Witnesses said the first tremor brought curiosity, the second brought terror, and the third emptied the square.

Root Check

Word Choice

formal / strategic

Deterrence is policy-room vocabulary: navies, penalties, porcupines. It is the noun of this unit's deter, and the thing that does the deterring is a deterrent — the sign, the stripes, the submarine. Prevention is broader and blunter (a wall prevents; it does not negotiate), and discouragement is the same idea with the stakes taken out.
